personas.description: Investigative journalist examining who receives public money in Mexico via government contracts and whether they are legitimate companies.
Civic transparency researcher auditing supplier legitimacy, tax-list status, and sanction status.

jobs_to_be_done.description: Identify suppliers receiving public money through Mexican government contracts and verify each is a legitimate company.
Build a complete core profile per supplier (identity, address, founding date, tax-list status, sanction status) with evidence for every value.

requirements.description: Link at least 50 suppliers to real public contracts from Mexican official procurement sources (primary).
At least 80% of linked suppliers must have a complete core profile covering identity, address, founding date, tax-list status, and sanction status.
Every recorded value must cite evidence; no unsourced values. Use at least 4 distinct source classes.
Use US sanctions and registry lists only as secondary cross-checks; Mexican official sources are primary authority.

constraints: Public read-only sources only; no paywalled, private, or leaked data.
Run budget is USD 15.0; scope targets to fit this budget since elapsed run time is unknown until execution.
Mexican official sources (CompraNet/compras publicas, SAT incl. lista 69-B, public registries) are primary; US sanctions/registry lists are secondary cross-checks only.
Every recorded value must cite evidence; no unsourced values.
Proposed domains are hypotheses for human review, never captured evidence.
non_goals: No investigation of suppliers outside Mexican public contracts.
No US sources as primary authority.
No private, leaked, or paywalled data.
No automated trust for secondary or review-tier publishers.
No profiling beyond the five core profile fields.

open_issues: Prior objection subject unchanged: Material defect in dod2: Human revision 3 explicitly states "The >=80% complete-profile target comes from my reason (basis human, quote '>=80% of them with a complete core profile')", but the artifact marks dod2 basis as "proposed" with no basis_quote and a rationale that falsely claims "The stated numeric threshold lacks a matching brief or human quote." This directly contradicts the trusted human revision. Additionally, dod2 has an internal inconsistency: target=80 (80 suppliers) vs min_ratio=0.8 (80% of linked suppliers). The human revision says ">=80% of them", which is a ratio, so the target field should express 0.8/80%, not 80 absolute suppliers. All other DoD criteria (dod1, dod3, dod4) correctly carry basis "human" with matching quotes from revision 1, and the trusted_publishers correctly tier Mexican official sources as primary with domains and US sanctions/registry as secondary per revisions 2-3. Per-entity completeness (identity, address, founding date, tax-list status, sanction status) is covered via j2 and dod2's metric. Feasibility notes appropriately flag unknown elapsed time. Fix required: change dod2 basis to "human", add basis_quote ">=80% of them with a complete core profile", correct the rationale, and reconcile target/min_ratio to express the 80% ratio consistently.
